Hans breaks off the chase and moves toward the reserve's open entry. Watching the retreating witness is briefly satisfying, but following farther would spend the opening on someone who cannot stop him now.

“Run, then. You were never the business I came here to finish.”

The remark preserves his superiority more cheaply than another pursuit. He keeps his attention on the route rather than trying to turn the witness's retreat into a surrender. Exposure has cost him concealment; it need not cost him access as well. He approaches the entry to attempt the corruption while it remains available, still alert to a real obstruction rather than committed to winning the abandoned chase.

Hans turns sharply toward the witness's route to the lever, trying to place his mobile body between the witness and the closure. The person's apparent weakness no longer makes the diversion irrelevant.

“Leave that alone. Walk away while you still have the choice.”

He would rather use the open entry than fight here, but ignoring this movement could remove the opportunity altogether. His threat is meant to buy a hesitation; he does not wait on the assumption that it must work. He tries to intercept the approach before returning to the reserve. The immediate target has changed because it now obstructs the plan, not because Hans has acquired a personal need to chase everyone.

He begins to invoke noninterference, then stops at the exception he has already read. The admission has given the colleague a reason to act that the general promise cannot simply remove.

“Our arrangement still matters. Before you stop the project, hear what I am proposing.”

He tries to keep the discussion on terms he can influence, minimizing the admission's significance rather than offering an unqualified confession or assuming forgiveness. At the same time, he prepares to withdraw from the immediate conversation if the colleague begins using that authority. He wants to preserve room to maneuver. The appeal is calculated, but he cannot make the exception disappear by repeating the broader promise more confidently.

He returns to the promise instead of volunteering a new restriction upon it. The colleague's authority is precisely why the agreement is worth invoking now.

“You gave your word that you would not interfere. I am asking whether that still means what it said.”

He leaves the question pointedly open, trying to turn uncertainty into a commitment before the colleague announces a decision. He has little reason to present the civilian harm as a reason to abandon his own project. Yet the written promise is a bargaining position, not knowledge of what the colleague will actually do. He watches for that answer and keeps withdrawal possible rather than treating the silence as guaranteed protection.

Hans detaches the available fragment and tries to throw it toward the entry, leaving the frozen portions where they are. Saving every part of himself is less useful at this instant than keeping a route to the target open.

“Keep watching this part of me. It may be the wrong part.”

He tries to draw the approaching opponent's attention to the restrained body while the small piece travels. He has no certainty that the distraction will last or that the fragment will arrive. The attempt costs material, but the material is available and the main body cannot advance. He commits to that narrow opportunity before demanding that the freeze somehow release him.

Hans tests the restraint, finds no usable part to release, and turns to speech as the opponent approaches. His usual bodily escape offers him nothing he can act on in this position.

“Wait. Is stopping me all you want? Then hear me before you decide what to do next.”

He tries to slow the confrontation with a question and an offered conversation, hoping the opponent has some interest he can use. The hope does not give him knowledge of that interest. He is angry at having the target so close and no remaining material route to it. For the moment, he spends his effort on obtaining time rather than claiming that the same frozen body has suddenly become free.
